# canary edge tests option_buys_after_regime_warning · COLUMNS=80 · LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 · colour off
Forward tests · option_buys_after_regime_warning · collecting

  Do single-name option buys made the session after a Regime warning do better
  or worse than the rest?
    helps with buying · tests no limit from your written policy
    registered 21 Nov 2026 07:00 TZ · rule text fingerprint 1d675e9bffa62dcc
    needs 40 after a warning, on 20 separate days
    checks Regime's stage at the last close
    counts each contract once per week with a buy, when its position has closed
    after a warning          ███▋░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    6 of 40   +2 waiting
      on separate days       ██████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░    5 of 20
    after any other session  ████████▍                  14         +3 waiting
    cannot be sorted         █▎                          2
      Canary has no Regime record for the close before them
    at this pace             █▄█  most 2 a month       full about Apr 2028
      more than a year away, and Canary counts only the last 365 days: this
      count cannot fill in this version
    a buy now counts as after a warning: Regime was at early warning at the 19
      Mar 2027 close
    waiting: SYNA 270115C00050000 15 Mar 2027, SYNB 270219C00030000 16 Mar 2027
    not counted: 2 part of a spread

  In short
    Each single-name option contract you buy counts once per week, once its
    position has closed. Its result is the average price you later sold at
    (zero if it expired), less the price you paid, after the buy's costs. Buys
    made the session after a Regime warning (early warning, confirmed stress or
    panic) are compared with all other such buys. No pass mark is set: the
    answer is a direction, looked at in the earlier and the later half of the
    buys. It is answered once, at 40 buys after a warning that fall on at least
    20 separate days. An option traded as part of a spread is left out.

  The rule as registered
    Single-name option buys that open or add to a long position, made in the
    session after a Regime warning, against all other such buys. A single name
    is any underlying but SPY and VIX. One reading per contract and week, final
    when its position has closed: the average price of the position's sales
    after the buy, zero at expiry, less the price paid, on the contracts
    bought, after the buy's costs. A position closed by delivery gives no
    reading. The figure for each group is the sum of its readings divided by
    the premium paid for them. The label is Regime's stage of the session
    before the buy: warning is early warning, confirmed stress or panic; the
    rest is quiet, stabilization or opportunity. No pass threshold is set for
    this test; it is read by direction in both the earlier and the later half
    of the readings by date. Read once, at 40 final readings after a warning
    session that fall on at least 20 separate days. An option traded in the
    same order as another option on the same underlying, as a spread is, is
    left out.
